subject.title: [Feature]: Track data provenance across session boundaries for persistent state

question: Should OpenClaw add a core/plugin-API provenance chain for durable state writes and reads, and what metadata may be persisted or exposed to plugins?
rationale: The remaining work defines a security boundary, public plugin contracts, persisted schema, migration behavior, and read-time trust policy, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent API shape.

options.title: Design Minimal Provenance API First
options.body: Keep this issue open for a maintainer/security design that specifies metadata, plugin visibility, migration behavior, and read-time policy before implementation.

options.title: Resolve Hook Prerequisites First
options.body: Settle the before_tool_call provenance and before_persistence_write hook proposals first, then revisit durable cross-session provenance once those contracts are stable.

options.title: Fold Into Security Umbrella
options.body: Move the remaining durable-provenance requirements under the broader persistent-taint/security architecture issue if maintainers want one canonical umbrella.

recommendation.title: Design Minimal Provenance API First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for a maintainer/security design that specifies metadata, plugin visibility, migration behavior, and read-time policy before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history signal across inter-session provenance, current hook types, external-content wrapping, and memory schema lines in this checkout.
